title: Trump: Hussain Sajwani pledges $20 billion to U.S. data centers
description_short: Trump: Hussain Sajwani pledges $20 billion to U.S. data centers
description_medium: Donald Trump announced that Emirati businessman Hussain Sajwani had pledged $20 billion for U.S. data centers, with an initial phase named for eight states. The announcement describes a private investment commitment, not completed construction or spending. The supplied account gives no project schedules, financing terms or evidence that funds were transferred.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Hussain Sajwani pledges $20 billion to U.S. data centers
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Hussain Sajwani pledges $20 billion to U.S. data centers

notes: Needs context: the supplied report gives the pledge amount and initial states but no project schedules, financing terms, site agreements or follow-through; the linked Reuters page returned HTTP 401 and the TrumpFile page returned HTTP 202.
Proposed correction: describe this as a private pledge unless later records establish investment or construction.

title: Trump: Report: Canadian authorities probing Tesla over suspicious-sales surge
description_short: Trump: Report: Canadian authorities probing Tesla over suspicious-sales surge
description_medium: A supplied account says Tesla reported 8,600 vehicle sales at four Canadian locations over three days, corresponding to $43 million in government rebates, around the suspension of an electric-vehicle rebate program. It says Canadian authorities were investigating the surge. The record provides no official statement or finding, and the figures alone do not establish improper claims.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Report: Canadian authorities probing Tesla over suspicious-sales surge
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Report: Canadian authorities probing Tesla over suspicious-sales surge

notes: Needs context: the linked TrumpFile page returned HTTP 202, and the supplied excerpt does not identify the investigating authority, its evidence, Tesla’s response or any finding.
Proposed correction: retain the sales figures as reported and describe the matter as an inquiry unless official records support fraud or improper rebate claims.

title: Trump: SEC drops suit against lawbreaking crypto company owned by Trump donor
description_short: Trump: SEC drops suit against lawbreaking crypto company owned by Trump donor
description_medium: Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong announced in February 2025 that the SEC had dropped its 2023 lawsuit alleging the exchange operated as an unregistered securities broker. The withdrawal ended that case but was not a court finding that Coinbase had violated the law. The supplied material does not show that donor status influenced the SEC’s decision.
description_long: On February 21, 2025, Coinbase chief executive Brian Armstrong announced that the Securities and Exchange Commission had dropped its lawsuit against the cryptocurrency exchange. The SEC had filed the case in June 2023, alleging that Coinbase operated as an unregistered securities broker. That was a civil enforcement allegation, not a final court finding that the company broke the law. The SEC’s decision ended that particular suit, but the supplied account does not explain whether it was dismissed with prejudice or what happened to other regulatory matters. The headline calls Coinbase a lawbreaking company owned by a Trump donor, yet the entry names neither the donor nor evidence that a donation affected the agency’s choice. It also does not establish that a single donor owned Coinbase or controlled the company. The documented event is the SEC’s withdrawal of its case; claims about ownership, a legal finding and political influence require separate support. Without those details, the timing of the dismissal alone does not establish an exchange of favors.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: SEC drops suit against lawbreaking crypto company owned by Trump donor
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: SEC drops suit against lawbreaking crypto company owned by Trump donor

notes: Needs context: the focused TrumpFile page returned HTTP 202; the supplied material does not name the alleged donor or support the headline’s ownership, lawbreaking or influence claims.
Proposed correction: describe Coinbase as the defendant in an SEC civil case that was dropped, and remove or substantiate the donor-ownership claim.

title: Trump: ICE uses online blacklist to target anti-war student protestors
description_short: Trump: ICE uses online blacklist to target anti-war student protestors
description_medium: A supplied summary of July court testimony by DHS official Peter Hatch says analysts formed a “Tiger Team” to review student protesters, used Canary Mission and another list, and prepared reports on more than 5,000 people. The account says information moved through Homeland Security Investigations to the State Department for possible removal decisions; final enforcement outcomes are not supplied.
description_long: A supplied summary of July court testimony by senior Department of Homeland Security official Peter Hatch describes analysts forming a “Tiger Team” to review student protesters. According to that account, the team used names from Canary Mission and another list and produced reports on more than 5,000 people. Information went through Homeland Security Investigations, which sent material to the State Department for possible removal decisions, according to the supplied account. Hatch reportedly said he had received verbal direction to consult Canary Mission, though he did not consider it an authoritative source; the summary also says speech such as “free Palestine” was among the phrases discussed. The account raises questions about how online material and political expression entered immigration review. It does not establish that every person named faced enforcement, that anyone was removed, or that the online list itself determined a case. The linked timeline summarizes testimony but does not include the transcript, formal unit order, full list of people reviewed or records of resulting decisions. Those documents are needed to establish the unit’s mandate, the scale of its work and what consequences followed.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: ICE uses online blacklist to target anti-war student protestors
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: ICE uses online blacklist to target anti-war student protestors

notes: Needs context: the linked timeline attributes these details to Hatch’s July court testimony, but the supplied material does not include the transcript, formal order, list of people reviewed or enforcement outcomes.
Proposed correction: attribute the reported process to Hatch’s testimony and avoid describing the list as a formal blacklist unless the underlying records establish that status.

title: Trump and Qatar bolster ties after jet bribe
description_short: Trump and Qatar bolster ties after jet bribe
description_medium: During Donald Trump’s May 2025 visit to Qatar, officials announced economic and defense agreements, and Qatar Airways said it intended to buy 210 Boeing aircraft. The supplied account also refers to a separate jet gift, but does not give its terms or evidence connecting it to the commercial announcements. Those deals alone do not establish a bribe.

preserved_fields.title: Trump and Qatar bolster ties after jet bribe
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump and Qatar bolster ties after jet bribe

notes: Needs context: the supplied synopsis mentions the 210-plane purchase and other agreements but does not give their terms or the separate jet gift’s details, ownership, conditions or timing; the linked TrumpFile page returned HTTP 202.
Proposed correction: treat the announced purchases as commercial agreements and reserve the word “bribe” for a supported account of the jet transfer and any quid pro quo.
